what: partially weighted local branch-mismatch sums in intermediate Rydberg units. NEITHER aggregate below is a physical error estimate; see per_call_group_l1_note and cross_group_warning.
units: intermediate Rydberg (vcoul carries the Ry scale; ssx and sch are dimensionless). NOT eV: the ryd conversion is applied later, and differently for diagonal and offdiagonal elements.
source: BerkeleyGW 4.0 Si-EPM GPP, fermi_level_absolute probe (charge-inconsistent); see bgw/weighted_audit/REVIEW_PACKET.md
weight: aqsntemp(ig,n1) * MYCONJG(aqsmtemp(igp,n1)) * vcoul(igp); real flavor, MYCONJG is the identity

both output types.neq(irq): q-star degeneracy; diagonal at Sigma/sigma_main.f90:1586-1587, offdiagonal at :1860-1861. Not available inside mtxel_cor.
both output types.sum over q-points: performed in sigma_main, outside this kernel
both output types.ax (bare exchange): separate term, not part of sigma_gpp_cpu
both output types.achcor (static remainder): separate term, not part of sigma_gpp_cpu

diagonal (icalc=1) only.ryd: applied in Sigma/shiftenergy.f90:113 as part of fact = ryd/dble(ndeg(ii))
diagonal (icalc=1) only.1/ndeg: degeneracy average, Sigma/shiftenergy.f90:113. The degenerate subspaces are built at :69 by a loop over `sig%ndiag` only, so this factor applies to DIAGONAL elements and not to offdiagonal ones.

offdiagonal (icalc=2) only.ryd: applied earlier, at Sigma/sigma_main.f90:1860-1861, together with neq; offdiagonal elements receive no 1/ndeg average

exported_records_vs_counted_events.relationship: Cardinality and id-sequentiality match the validated tally. Completeness -- that these records ARE the counted population rather than a same-sized different set -- additionally requires the shared-predicate and same-run-provenance links in completeness_evidence, which this program does not check.

completeness_evidence.checked here: cardinality equals the validated tally's near-pole occ != 1 count, and record ids are exactly 1..N with no duplicates
completeness_evidence.not checked here (1) shared predicate: counting and emission happen at two sites in the same inner loop of sigma_gpp_cpu, both gated on the same derived predicate `t4_b == 2 .and. t4_o == 2`, so a counted event and an emitted record are the same event. Verifiable by reading bgw/weighted_audit/t004_instrument.patch.
completeness_evidence.not checked here (2) same-run provenance: the saved tally file and the saved record file were written by the same instrumented execution of the same binary. Verifiable from bgw/weighted_audit/PROVENANCE*.txt.
completeness_evidence.conclusion: cardinality alone does not establish completeness; it does so only together with (1) and (2), which are documentary rather than checked by this program

comparator_note: branch_mismatch compares two expressions at identical inputs; it is not a counterfactual program run, and it ignores any sexcut difference in the generic branch

local_reconstruction_check.meaning: the Fortran summed K*L itself, in its own arithmetic, over exactly these records, and the Python subtotal agrees. This validates the GROUPED SUBTOTAL in two arithmetic implementations. It does NOT independently validate any individual captured weight or local value, nor bound their individual reconstruction errors: per-term errors can cancel within a subtotal

per_call_group_l1_note: A CHOSEN DATASET L1 NORM over per-call accumulator groups, not a preferred physical effect size. Each per-call-accumulator-group signed mismatch is taken in magnitude before aggregating, so cancellation between groups is avoided WITHIN THIS DIAGNOSTIC. That is a property of the choice, not evidence that such cancellation is unphysical: BerkeleyGW deliberately sums related q-point and call contributions, with their outer factors, on the way to a self-energy. Neither this L1 norm nor cross_group_signed_over_accumulators is a physical error estimate. Quote it as a per-call L1 diagnostic or not at all.
cross_group_warning: The signed counterpart: the signed sum over all groups divided by the accumulator total, so different calls, matrix elements, q-points and iw energies do cancel against one another. It is reported for comparison with the L1 norm. It is likewise NOT a physical error estimate, and the difference between the two numbers measures how much this dataset cancels internally, not which of them is physically correct.
reference_warning: total_signed_over_local uses the exported records' OWN local contribution as the reference, which is a small subset of the accumulator, so the ratio is not informative about size. The two aggregates that divide by the accumulators instead are per_call_group_l1_over_accumulators and cross_group_signed_over_accumulators. Neither is preferred and neither is a physical error estimate; read them together.
